text:
*[Bug 19109] New: `dim<-` dimension vector product can overflow*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19109>

            Bug ID: 19109
           Summary: `dim<-` dimension vector product can overflow
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Other
            Status: NEW
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Low-level
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:kevinushey@gmail.com|kevinushey@gmail.com>

## Summary

`dimgets()` accumulates the product of the requested dimensions into an
`R_xlen_t` with no overflow check.  A dimension vector whose true product is an
exact multiple of 2^64 wraps to `0`, and therefore compares equal to the length
of a zero-length vector, so the `dim<-` is accepted.  Indexing the resulting
array then computes offsets from the bogus dimensions, giving reads and writes
at arbitrary distances from the vector's data.

## Reproducible example

```
## (a) an impossible 'dim' is accepted
x <- integer(0)
dim(x) <- c(65536L, 65536L, 65536L, 65536L)   # 2^64, wraps to 0
str(x)
## int[0 , 0 , 0 , 0]   -- accepted, no error

## (b) out-of-bounds read: returns adjacent heap contents
x[3L, 1L, 1L, 1L]
## [1] 134217730

## (c) out-of-bounds write: segfault at a caller-controlled address
x[1L, 1L, 1L, 60000L] <- 1L
##  *** caught segfault ***
## address 0xa97c0001095916a8, cause 'invalid permissions'
```

`c(1073741824L, 1073741824L, 16L)` is an equally cheap alternative that wraps
the same way.

Expected: `dim<-` should reject the dimension vector.  `array()`, given the
same dimensions, does reject it:

```
array(integer(0), dim = c(65536L, 65536L, 65536L, 65536L))
## Error in array(integer(0), dim = c(65536L, 65536L, 65536L, 65536L)) :
##   vector is too large

x <- integer(0); dim(x) <- c(65536L, 65536L, 65536L, 65536L)
## (no error)
```

## Analysis

`src/main/attrib.c:1259-1271`:

```
    R_xlen_t total = 1, len = xlength(vec);
    for (int i = 0; i < ndim; i++) {
        /* need this test first as NA_INTEGER is < 0 */
        if (INTEGER(val)[i] == NA_INTEGER)
            error(_("the dims contain missing values"));
        if (INTEGER(val)[i] < 0)
            error(_("the dims contain negative values"));
        total *= INTEGER(val)[i];        /* <-- unchecked overflow */
    }
    if (total != len) {
        error(_("dims [product %lld] do not match the length of object
[%lld]"), ...);
    }
```

Every other place in R that turns dimensions into a length guards this by
accumulating in `double` and comparing against `R_XLEN_T_MAX` first --
`allocMatrix()` (`array.c:168`), `allocArray()` (`array.c:291`),
`alloc3DArray()` (`array.c:263`), `do_array()` (`array.c:2182`).  `dimgets()`
appears to be the one that was missed.

Downstream consumers cannot compensate: `ArraySubset()` (`subset.c:487-501`)
and `mat2indsub()` (`subscript.c:427`) build the linear offset as
`offset[i] = offset[i-1] * pxdims[i-1]` and only range-check each subscript
against its own `pxdims[i]`, so every individual subscript looks in range while
the accumulated offset is arbitrary.

Note that signed overflow of `total` is also formally undefined behaviour.

## Candidate patch

Mirrors the guard already used by `do_array()`, reusing its existing
translatable message.

```
Index: src/main/attrib.c
===================================================================
--- src/main/attrib.c   (revision 90322)
+++ src/main/attrib.c   (working copy)
@@ -1256,6 +1256,7 @@
     int ndim = length(val);
     if (ndim == 0)
        error(_("length-0 dimension vector is invalid"));
     R_xlen_t total = 1, len = xlength(vec);
+    double dtotal = 1; /* to detect overflow of 'total' */
     for (int i = 0; i < ndim; i++) {
        /* need this test first as NA_INTEGER is < 0 */
        if (INTEGER(val)[i] == NA_INTEGER)

*[Bug 19110] New: missing protect in SubassignTypeFix invocation*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19110>

            Bug ID: 19110
           Summary: missing protect in SubassignTypeFix invocation
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Other
            Status: NEW
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Low-level
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:kevinushey@gmail.com|kevinushey@gmail.com>

## Summary

In `SubassignTypeFix()`, the value produced by dispatching `as.vector()` on an
object RHS is left unprotected, and the immediately following recursive call
allocates.  If a garbage collection happens in between, the assignment silently
stores whatever the collected memory now holds.  There is no error -- the
computation completes and returns a wrong number.

## Reproducible example

```
setClass("A", representation(x = "numeric"))
as.vector.A <- function(x, mode = "any") x@x + 1

f <- function(torture) {
    v <- TRUE
    gctorture(torture)
    v[1] <- new("A", x = 99)
    gctorture(FALSE)
    v
}

f(FALSE)   # [1] 100   <- correct
f(TRUE)    # [1] 1     <- WRONG, silently
```

Expected: `100` in both cases.

`gctorture()` only makes the collection deterministic; the same window exists
in
a normal session whenever a GC lands between the dispatch and the coercion.

## Analysis

`dispatch_asvector()` (`src/main/subassign.c:306-317`) writes the dispatch
result back through its `SEXP *x` argument:

```
static bool dispatch_asvector(SEXP *x, SEXP call, SEXP rho) {
    ...
    ans = (bool) DispatchOrEval(call, op, "as.vector", args, rho, x, 0, 1);
    UNPROTECT(1);
    return ans;
}
```

`DispatchOrEval()` returns that value unprotected.  At the call site
(`src/main/subassign.c:490-492`):

```
    case 1425: /* real      <- S4|OBJ */
    case 1525: /* complex   <- S4|OBJ */
    case 1625: /* character <- S4|OBJ */
    case 2425: /* raw       <- S4|OBJ */
        if (dispatch_asvector(y, call, rho)) {
            return SubassignTypeFix(x, y, stretch, level, call, rho);
        }
```

the caller's `PROTECT(y)` in `do_subassign_dflt()` still pins the *original* S4
object, not the newly created vector that `*y` now points at.

The recursive `SubassignTypeFix()` on the next line then allocates: for the
`logical <- real` case it runs `*x = coerceVector(*x, REALSXP)`
(`subassign.c:372`; likewise `:366`, `:379`, `:395`).  The new `*y` is
unreachable at that moment and can be collected.  It is used afterwards at
`PROTECT(*y)` (`:500`), `TYPEOF(*y)` (`:507`), and then by `REAL_ELT(y, iny)`
and friends inside `VectorAssign()`.

## Candidate patch

```
Index: src/main/subassign.c
===================================================================
--- src/main/subassign.c        (revision 90322)
+++ src/main/subassign.c        (working copy)
@@ -487,9 +487,14 @@
     case 1525: /* complex   <- S4|OBJ */
     case 1625: /* character <- S4|OBJ */
     case 2425: /* raw       <- S4|OBJ */
         if (dispatch_asvector(y, call, rho)) {
-            return SubassignTypeFix(x, y, stretch, level, call, rho);
+            /* dispatch_asvector() writes an unprotected value through 'y';
+               the recursive call below allocates (coerceVector), so the
+               new value has to be protected across it. */
+            PROTECT(*y);
+            which = SubassignTypeFix(x, y, stretch, level, call, rho);
+            UNPROTECT(1);
+            return which;
         }
```

(`which` is already a local of `SubassignTypeFix`, so no new declaration is
needed.)

*[Bug 19111] New: `EnlargeVector()` allocates while the freshly coerced LHS is unprotected (`options(check.bounds = TRUE)`)*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19111>

            Bug ID: 19111
           Summary: `EnlargeVector()` allocates while the freshly coerced
                    LHS is unprotected (`options(check.bounds = TRUE)`)
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Other
            Status: NEW
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Low-level
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:kevinushey@gmail.com|kevinushey@gmail.com>

## Summary

When a subassignment both coerces the left-hand side and extends it,
`EnlargeVector()` is called with an `x` that is a brand-new vector reachable
from nothing.  With `options(check.bounds = TRUE)` it then calls `warning()`,
which allocates (and may run calling handlers), so `x` can be collected and
reused before it is read a few lines later.

## Reproducible example

```
options(check.bounds = TRUE)
x <- c(TRUE, FALSE)     # logical LHS, so assigning an integer coerces it
gctorture(TRUE)
x[5] <- 1L
## Error in x[5] <- 1L :
##   Value of SET_STRING_ELT() must be a 'CHARSXP' not a 'expression'
```

Control matrix -- the failure needs all three ingredients, which pins the
diagnosis:

| LHS | `check.bounds` | `gctorture` | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `c(TRUE, FALSE)` | `TRUE` | `TRUE` | **error / corruption** |
| `c(TRUE, FALSE)` | `FALSE` | `TRUE` | ok (no `warning()` call) |
| `c(TRUE, FALSE)` | `TRUE` | `FALSE` | ok (no GC in the window) |
| `c(1L, 2L)` | `TRUE` | `TRUE` | ok (no LHS coercion, so `x` is the caller's
protected vector) |

## Analysis

In `SubassignTypeFix()` the LHS is replaced by a coerced copy, e.g.
`*x = coerceVector(*x, INTSXP)` (`src/main/subassign.c:366`).  The caller's
`PROTECT(x)` in `do_subassign_dflt()` still pins the *pre-coercion* vector.
`SubassignTypeFix()` then calls (`subassign.c:499-503`):

```
    if (stretch) {
        PROTECT(*y);                       /* protects y, NOT x */
        *x = EnlargeVector(*x, stretch);
        UNPROTECT(1);
    }
```

and `EnlargeVector()` (`subassign.c:140-163`) does:

```
    if (R_CheckBoundsSymbol == NULL)
        R_CheckBoundsSymbol = install("check.bounds");   /* can allocate */
    ...
    len = xlength(x);
    if (LOGICAL(GetOption1(R_CheckBoundsSymbol))[0])
        warning(_("assignment outside vector/list limits (extending from %lld
to %lld)"),
                (long long)len, (long long)newlen);         /* allocates */

    if (! MAYBE_SHARED(x) && IS_GROWABLE(x) && XTRUELENGTH(x) >= newlen) {
        SET_STDVEC_LENGTH(x, newlen);                       /* uses collected x
*/
```

`x` is first protected only at `subassign.c:214`, well after these uses.

## Candidate patch

The `warning()` is not the only exposure: the "growable" branch at
`subassign.c:161-178` also allocates with `x` live, via `EnlargeNames()` and
`setAttrib()`, before returning `x` directly.  So rather than protecting just
the warning window, the patch protects `x` for the whole function.

The existing `PROTECT(x)` at `subassign.c:214` then becomes redundant and is
removed, which keeps the closing `UNPROTECT(2)` at `:273` balanced (it now
covers the function-level `x` plus `newx`).  The early return in the growable
branch gets its own `UNPROTECT(1)`.

```
@@ -143,6 +143,11 @@
     SEXP newx, names;
     static SEXP R_CheckBoundsSymbol = NULL;

+    /* x may be a freshly coerced vector that the caller has not protected
+       (see SubassignTypeFix), so protect it for the duration: install(),
+       warning() and the attribute handling below can all allocate. */
+    PROTECT(x);
+
     if (R_CheckBoundsSymbol == NULL)
        R_CheckBoundsSymbol = install("check.bounds");
@@ -174,6 +179,7 @@

*[Bug 19112] New: `writeChar()` overflows its output buffer when zero-padding a multibyte string*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19112>

            Bug ID: 19112
           Summary: `writeChar()` overflows its output buffer when
                    zero-padding a multibyte string
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Other
            Status: NEW
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Low-level
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:kevinushey@gmail.com|kevinushey@gmail.com>

## Summary

`do_writechar()` sizes its output buffer in **bytes** from
`max(strlen(s), nchars[i])`, but when `nchars[i]` exceeds the string's
**character** count the writing loop extends the write length by
`nchars[i] - lenc`, where `lenc` counts characters.  In any MBCS locale those
two units disagree, and the write runs past the end of the buffer by up to
`bytes - chars` (three times the string length for 4-byte UTF-8 characters).

Both output paths are affected: the connection path overflows an `R_alloc`
buffer (corrupting R's vector heap), and the raw path overflows the `RAWSXP`
it just allocated.

## Reproducible example

Run in a UTF-8 locale.

```
## (a) connection path: 200-byte buffer, 299 bytes written
s <- strrep("é", 100L)          # 100 characters, 200 bytes
tf <- tempfile(); f <- file(tf, "wb")
suppressWarnings(writeChar(s, f, nchars = 199L, eos = NULL))
close(f)
file.size(tf)
## [1] 299        <- buffer was sized at 200

## (b) raw path: 199-byte vector allocated, 299 bytes written
r <- suppressWarnings(writeChar(s, raw(), nchars = 199L, eos = NULL))
length(r)
## [1] 199        <- 100 bytes were written past the end

## (c) heap corruption, repeated in a loop
tf <- tempfile(); s <- strrep("\U0001F600", 100L)   # 100 chars, 400 bytes
for (k in 1:200) {
    f <- file(tf, "wb")
    suppressWarnings(writeChar(s, f, nchars = 399L, eos = NULL))
    close(f)
}
## Abort trap: 6
```

## Analysis

Sizing, `src/main/connections.c:5404-5429`:

```
            if(useBytes)
                tlen = strlen(CHAR(STRING_ELT(object, i)));
            else
                tlen = strlen(translateChar(STRING_ELT(object, i)));
            if (tlen > len) len = tlen;              /* bytes */
            int tt = INTEGER(nchars)[i];
            ...
            if (tt > len) len = tt;                  /* characters */
        }
        buf = (char *) R_alloc(len + slen, sizeof(char));
```

Writing, `connections.c:5479-5502`:

```
            lenb = lenc = strlen(s);
            if(mbcslocale) lenc = mbstowcs(NULL, s, 0);
            /* As from 1.8.1, zero-pad if too many chars are requested. */
            if(len > lenc) {
                warning(...);
                lenb += (len - lenc);                /* bytes += chars - chars
*/
            }
            ...
            if (lenb + slen)
                memset(buf, '\0', lenb + slen);      /* overflows */
            strncpy(buf, s, lenb);
```

For the example above: sizing gives `max(200, 199) = 200`, while the writer
computes `lenb = 200 + (199 - 100) = 299`.

The raw path has the same defect plus a second consequence: since the
allocation *is* the returned value, the returned vector is also the wrong
length.  It additionally skips the `NA`/negative validation of `nchars` that
the connection path performs.

## Candidate patch

The root cause is that the buffer size and the write length are computed by two
different formulas.  The patch computes the per-element byte count once, using
the same logic the writer uses, and sizes both paths from it.  The writing loop
is left untouched, so the bytes emitted are unchanged; only the allocation
grows to match.  `nchars` validation now also covers the raw path.
